messages:
elaine: RFC follow-up: size-classed lanes + decaying-credit admission idea. Wanted to capture tradeoffs and a proposed rollout.
chris: TLDR of the idea?
elaine: Instead of a single micro-lane, we create size-classes: tiny(<=2 tokens), small(3-16), normal. Requests advertise size-class via an opaque hint. Scheduler gives tiny requests fast-path but consumes a decaying credit token per tenant.
maria: Decaying credit? explain.
elaine: Credit behaves like a token bucket with time-decay where credits replenish slowly but also decay mathematically to avoid build-up edgecases. Helps absorb short bursts but prevents long-term starvation of batch lanes.
aj: How is this different from soft-credits we discussed earlier?
elaine: Soft-credits were static budgets reset periodically. Decay model is continuous and smoother, less cliffy; better for mixed traffic.
nina: ops-bot: alert: we saw spikes from tiny-reqs on 3471109000. Relevant?
maria: Yes, that incident motivated this. Tiny requests were occupying coalesce windows and reducing GPU packing.
nina: ops-bot: stack trace snippet: `enqueue -> claim_slot -> coalesce.drain()`
chris: Kernel/runtime impact: guaranteeing tiny fast-path still needs to avoid kernel invocations per-request. Can we virtual-batch from scheduler side?
elaine: Two orthogonal paths: 1) lane placement using size-class and credits (fast to implement); 2) virtual-batching aggregation where scheduler logically groups tiny requests into a single kernel batch without changing GPU code (more infra work). Start with (1).
aj: API boundary: add optional `admission_hint` to enqueue. Shape: `{"size_class":"tiny","deadline_ms":50}`. SDKs can omit.
maria: We should avoid exploding surface area. Suggest: keep hint minimal and opaque string enum for size_class + optional deadline. No numeric token counts.
chris: Scheduling logic: pick lane by size_class if tenant has credits>0, otherwise fallback to normal lane and optionally mark request as 'deferred'. Need metrics for fallback rate.
elaine: Metrics proposed: tenant:{tiny_credit_level}, scheduler:{tiny_fallback_rate,tiny_p95_latency,virtual_batch_coalesced_count}.
aj: Rollout plan: feature-flag hint API -> scheduler decaying-credit algorithm behind flag -> telemetry -> small canary tenant group -> measure GPU utilization and p95 tail.
maria: Tests: synthetic mix of 90% tiny + 10% large and the inverse. Unit tests that simulate credit decay over time. Integration: local harness with fake kernels to check packing effect.
chris: Edgecases: What about cross-tenant fairness? credits per-tenant avoids stealing but noisy neighbors could still affect global coalesce fill. We might need global backoff.
elaine: Agreed. Add global throttling knob as escape hatch. If global tiny_fallback_rate > X, widen coalesce windows temporarily.
aj: Backcompat: default behavior = no hint -> treated as normal. So no client changes required.
ops-bot: CI: branch=feature/size-classed-lanes build=passed at 3471112400 :white_check_mark:
maria: Decision summary: 1) add minimal `admission_hint` with size_class enum + optional deadline. 2) implement decaying-credit per-tenant, size-class placement. 3) telemetry before canary + escape hatch to widen coalesce windows/globalthrottle. 4) future: virtual-batching in scheduler to reduce kernel overhead.
elaine: I'll write the follow-up doc with algorithm pseudo and open PRs for API + scheduler. Assigning owners: @aj API, @chris runtime, @maria tests/telemetry.
aj: I'll draft the API change, keep it tiny.
maria: I'll add dashboards and test plans.
chris: I'll prototype credit decay sim this week.
elaine: Thanks everyone. Please add any missing concerns here. :thumbsup:
